stories.label: DG ISPR says Pakistani troops present in Saudi Arabia 'for decades' across multiple domains
stories.summary: Pakistan's military spokesman, Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry, has confirmed on the record that Pakistani troops are in Saudi Arabia, saying they have been there 'for decades' and across multiple domains. Lead with the confirmation and what he said about their role, quoted exactly as Dawn gives it, and say where and to whom he gave the interview. The mechanism: the statement comes while Saudi Arabia is fighting Yemen's Houthis and days after reports that Pakistan and Turkey would deploy forces under the Mecca pact, so say what he confirmed and what he declined to say about numbers, combat roles and whether any troops are near the Yemen front, and what the defence agreement between the two states binds Pakistan to. One clause of context: the Houthi strike on Aden airport and the missile downed near Riyadh (covered 10-07). Who it lands on: Pakistani soldiers placed inside another country's war, a parliament that has not voted on it (only if Dawn says so), and Yemenis on the other side of the line. State nothing about deployments beyond what the spokesman said. Dawn is the regional outlet and the only source. Dateline Rawalpindi or Islamabad as the report supports.

stories.label: Kosovo swears in Shiroka-Pula as president, averting snap elections
stories.summary: Kosovo's parliament elected Justina Shiroka-Pula president and she was sworn in hours later, ending a deadlock that would otherwise have forced snap elections. Lead with the vote: how many votes she received against the threshold, in which round, and which parties supplied them. The mechanism: Kosovo's president is chosen by parliament, and a failure to elect one within the constitutional deadline dissolves the assembly, so the presidency is the lever by which an opposition can bring down a government; say how long the standoff ran, what was traded to end it, and what Prime Minister Albin Kurti, who called the result a sign of institutional stability, gains. Say who she is and whom she replaces, and explain the report's reference to The Hague and war crimes (the Kosovo Specialist Chambers) only as the report gives it. Who it lands on: a Muslim-majority state of under two million whose EU path and talks with Serbia stall whenever its institutions do. TRT World is Turkish state media and the only source: attribute the account to 'Turkish state broadcaster TRT World' and state as fact only the vote and the swearing-in. The 'Pula' tag is a mis-tag of her surname. Dateline Pristina.

stories.label: How the Dagalos' ever tightening hold on power destabilized the RSF project
stories.summary: Sudan's Rapid Support Forces have gained territory but are losing politically, Mada Masr reports, because the Dagalo family has concentrated command, money and the parallel government in its own hands. Lead with the most concrete recent fact the report gives: a defection, a split, a clash between allied factions or a dismissal, with names and dates. The mechanism: the RSF is a coalition of tribal militias, allied armed movements and civilian politicians held together by pay and promised shares of power, so say which posts and revenue streams (gold, border trade, foreign backing, as the report documents) the family has taken for itself, which allies have broken away or been pushed out, and what that does to the RSF's claim to govern the areas it holds. Who it lands on: civilians in Darfur and Kordofan living under that force, with the documented killings and displacement counted as the report gives them, and those under army control counted with the same care. This is a long reported piece: take the documented facts and leave the analysis attributed to the outlet or its named sources. The feed carried only a one-line summary, so write only what the fetched page supports. Mada Masr is the regional outlet and the only source, doing original reporting. Dateline Nyala, El Fasher or Port Sudan as the report supports.

stories.label: Britain helped to kill 'Zionism is Racism' resolution at the UN
stories.summary: British government files show the UK foreign secretary boasting of 'mounting a world wide lobbying exercise' to overturn the UN General Assembly's 1975 resolution that called Zionism a form of racism, Declassified UK reports. Lead with the document: who wrote it, when, to whom, and the words quoted. The mechanism: Resolution 3379 was revoked in 1991, the only time the General Assembly has rescinded one of its own resolutions, so say which governments Britain lobbied and how, what it offered or threatened as the files record, and how the vote went; say where the files are held and when they were released. Why now, in one clause: the question of who has equated Zionism with racism returned to British politics this week (covered 10-06), and this is the archival record of what the British state did about it. Who it lands on: Palestinians, whose case at the UN was shaped by that reversal. Declassified UK is an advocacy-forward outlet and the only source: state as fact only what the quoted documents say, attribute every reading of them to the outlet, and drop any claim the files do not support. No regional outlet in the feed carried it. Dateline London.

stories.label: Fed's Warsh Earns IMF Praise for Focusing on Price Stability
stories.summary: US inflation has been above the Federal Reserve's target for more than five and a half years, IMF managing director Kristalina Georgieva said, while praising Fed chair Kevin Warsh for keeping his focus on price stability. Lead with the five-and-a-half-year figure and who said it. The mechanism: when the lender of last resort to the world's governments publicly backs a central bank for holding rates high, it tells markets not to expect relief, on the day US long-bond yields touched their highest since 2002 with Brent crude above $100 (covered this morning, one clause); give what she said about long-term inflation expectations, government debt and artificial intelligence, and any IMF figures, only as the reports state them. Name the series plainly: US inflation and the Fed's policy rate. Who it lands on: borrowers in the United States and the developing countries whose dollar debt reprices with every month US rates stay high. TASS is Russian state media and carries the fuller text; Bloomberg is the independent source and may be paywalled, so quote Georgieva directly, attribute nothing to TASS's framing, and write only what the fetched pages support. Dateline where she spoke, as the reports give it (TASS datelines Tokyo; the feed tags Bangkok): not a US dateline.

stories.label: Iran has 'lost complete control' of Strait of Hormuz', US claims | The National
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Wednesday that Iran has 'lost complete control' of the Strait of Hormuz and that 'there's almost as much oil flowing out now as there was before this conflict', one day after a tanker was struck off Oman and its crew evacuated (covered 10-07). Lead with the claim set against that fact, and treat it as a claim: attribute it to Rubio throughout. The mechanism: the reader can check it, because this is ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and the price of Brent crude; say what evidence Rubio or US officials offered, what The National reports about actual tanker transits, insurance and who is escorting ships, and what Iran says in reply. Explain why Washington wants the strait declared open (oil above $100, bond yields at multi-decade highs) only as the report supports. Give what he said about the Houthis, Hezbollah and Hamas in one sentence at most. Who it lands on: the Gulf exporters and Iraq, whose revenue leaves through the strait, and the crews sailing it. The National (UAE) is the regional outlet and the only source. Dateline where Rubio spoke, as the report gives it; this is a Hormuz story, not a US dateline.

stories.label: India miffed over 'Ukrainian' drone strike on oil tanker
stories.summary: Follow-up to the 10-06 piece on the tanker set ablaze off Sochi (one clause). The new development: India's Ministry of External Affairs has responded formally to the strike on the Liberian-flagged Aframax Rio, calling for dialogue to safeguard seafarers and freedom of navigation, after all 23 crew, Indian citizens among them, were rescued. Lead with New Delhi's statement, quoted as the report gives it, and whether it names Ukraine; the headline's quotation marks around 'Ukrainian' matter, so say who attributes the drone to Kyiv and whether Kyiv has claimed it. The mechanism: India is the largest buyer of Russian seaborne crude and one of the largest suppliers of merchant crews, so Ukraine's campaign against Russia's oil exports now puts Indian nationals and Indian energy supply in the line of fire, twice in two days counting the tanker struck in the Strait of Hormuz with 11 Indians injured (covered 10-07, one clause). Say what the ship carried and for whom, and give any effect on Black Sea insurance or the price of Brent crude only as reported. Who it lands on: seafarers from labour-exporting countries on ships flagged elsewhere. Single source. Dateline New Delhi.

stories.label: UAE-EAEU trade pact takes effect, cutting tariffs on 95% of bilateral trade
stories.summary: A free trade agreement between the United Arab Emirates and the Eurasian Economic Union (Russia, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and Armenia) has taken effect, cutting tariffs on 95% of trade between them. Lead with the entry into force, the 95% figure and the size of the trade it covers. The mechanism: the pact gives Russia, under Western sanctions, a tariff-free channel into a Gulf re-export hub, and gives the UAE preferential access to a market of about 180 million people that Western firms have left; say which goods are covered and which are excluded, how fast tariffs fall, and what the agreement says about services, payments or rules of origin, as the report gives it. The structural point: trade is being rebuilt around the sanctions regime, not through it, by a US security partner. Who it lands on: Kazakh and Kyrgyz exporters as well as Russian ones, and Emirati traders and logistics firms. The feed entry had no summary, so write only what the fetched page supports and drop the story if the page yields too little. Single source; no other regional outlet in the feed carried it. Dateline Abu Dhabi or Dubai as the report supports.

stories.label: Neanderthal Europe was as much a wooden age as a stone age | New Scientist
stories.summary: Wooden tools, weapons, building materials and domestic items recovered from a cave in Spain show that Neanderthal technology rested on wood at least as much as on stone. Lead with the find: what the objects are, how many, how old, and which cave. The mechanism for a technical reader: wood almost never survives tens of thousands of years, so the archaeological record is biased toward stone and the 'Stone Age' is partly an artefact of preservation; say what conditions preserved these pieces, how they were dated, what tool marks or wear show about how they were made and used, and what skills that implies (choice of species, shaping, use of fire). Say what it changes about the picture of Neanderthal daily life and what the researchers say remains uncertain. Name the journal and the lead institution, attribute claims to the researchers, and add no figure the page does not give. Give the article a dateline and location: the town nearest the cave as the report names it, otherwise the lead institution's city.

stories.label: 194-year-old tortoise has exceptional DNA repair systems that fight off ageing | New Scientist
stories.summary: Scientists have sequenced the genome of Jonathan, a 194-year-old giant tortoise and the oldest known living land animal, and found that the parts of it governing mitochondrial function work as efficiently as those of a five-year-old of his species. Lead with that comparison. The mechanism for a technical reader: mitochondria produce the cell's energy and, as a by-product, the reactive molecules that damage DNA, so efficient mitochondria may leave his DNA repair systems less to do and more capacity to do it; say what was sequenced and compared against what, which genes or pathways stand out, and how the team separates cause from correlation in a sample of one animal. State the limits plainly: one individual, and a finding about a tortoise is not a therapy for humans, whatever the headlines say. Say what the researchers propose to test next. Name the journal and institutions, attribute claims to the researchers, and add no figure the pages do not give. 404 Media reported the same study and is merged in as a second source. Give the article a dateline and location: Jamestown, St Helena, where Jonathan lives, if the reports place him there, otherwise the lead institution's city.

stories.label: As AI Closed In on 'Unique Games' Proof, Researchers Raced to Beat the Machines
stories.summary: Three computer scientists rushed out a milestone result on the Unique Games Conjecture, one of the central open problems in theoretical computer science, because they had heard an AI system was close to a proof of its own. Lead with the result and the race: what they proved, and that the rumour of a machine proof set the deadline. The mechanism for a technical reader: say in two sentences what the conjecture claims (that for a broad class of optimisation problems, even finding a good approximate answer is computationally hard) and why so much of the theory of approximation rests on it, then what the new result establishes and how far it stops short of the full conjecture, as Quanta states it. On the AI side, say what is actually known: which system, who built it, whether any proof has been published or verified, and what remains rumour; state nothing about the AI proof as fact unless Quanta confirms it. The structural point: the norms of mathematical credit and pace are changing because researchers now compete with machines. The feed entry was a teaser, so write only what the fetched page supports. Single source. Give the article a dateline and location: the city of the lead researchers' institution as the page states it.

stories.label: First observation of quantum spins shifting a centimeter-scale object in the lab
stories.summary: Physicists report the first observation of quantum spins physically moving an object a centimetre across, large enough to see with the naked eye. Lead with what moved, by how much, and what moved it. The mechanism for a technical reader: spin is the quantum angular momentum carried by electrons or nuclei, and angular momentum is conserved, so flipping a very large number of spins together must make the body that holds them twist or shift (the Einstein-de Haas effect is the classical precedent; mention it only if the page does); say what the object was made of, how the spins were driven, how the displacement was measured, and how the team ruled out heating, magnetic forces and vibration. Say why it matters: a quantum property producing a mechanical effect at human scale, and what the authors say it could be used for (sensing, tests of quantum mechanics in large objects) and what is not yet shown. Phys.org carries a press summary and the feed entry was a teaser: name the journal and institutions, attribute claims to the researchers, add no figure the page does not give, and drop the story if the page yields too little. Give the article a dateline and location: the city of the lead institution as the page states it.

stories.label: Trade group crunches numbers on Trump's impossible push for 100% US-made tech
stories.summary: A technology trade group has put numbers on Donald Trump's goal of electronics made entirely in the United States, and finds it cannot be done at anything like current prices. Lead with the group's headline figure: what a fully US-made laptop or phone would cost, or how many years and dollars the supply chain would take to move, as Ars reports it. The mechanism for a technical reader: a finished device draws on components, materials and assembly spread over dozens of countries, so say which stages have no US capacity at all (displays, batteries, passive components, final assembly labour), what the group estimates each would cost to build, and what the 'Genesis Mission' executive order and the tariffs attached to it actually require. Say who the trade group represents: its members are the companies that would pay, so give the figures as its own and the administration's reply. Who it lands on: US buyers through prices, and the workers and economies of the Asian countries where these devices are made now. The 'Chicago Transit Authority' tag is a mis-tag of the trade group's initials. Single source. Dateline Washington. US dateline (1 of 3).

stories.label: Outstreaming Taylor Swift is easy with 10K bots and AI songs, fraudster admits
stories.summary: Michael Smith, 54, of North Carolina, was sentenced to 18 months in prison after pleading guilty to using AI-generated songs and about 10,000 bot accounts to take millions of dollars in royalties from music streaming platforms, the US Department of Justice says. Lead with the sentence and the scale: how many songs, how many streams, how much money, over how long. The mechanism for a technical reader: streaming services pay rights holders from a shared pool in proportion to plays, so every fake stream takes money from real musicians; say how he generated the catalogue, how the bots spread plays thinly across thousands of tracks to stay under fraud detection, how he was caught, and what he must forfeit. The structural point: generative AI makes the supply of tracks unlimited, and the pro-rata royalty model has no defence except detection. Say what the platforms have changed, if reported. Who it lands on: working musicians paid from the same pool. Single source. Dateline New York or the court's city as the report gives it. US dateline (2 of 3).

stories.label: Oklahoma judge's Flock ruling shows the power of Supreme Court's digital evidence decision
stories.summary: A federal judge in Oklahoma has thrown out evidence a sheriff obtained from Flock licence-plate cameras in a drug trafficking case, relying on the Supreme Court's recent Chatrie decision on geofence warrants. Lead with the ruling and why it is a first: a high-court decision about phone location data applied to a network of roadside cameras. The mechanism for a technical reader: say what Chatrie held about searching location databases without a warrant, how the judge reasoned that querying Flock's pooled record of where a car has been is the same kind of search, what the sheriff did (which searches, across how many cameras or agencies, with or without a warrant), and what the ruling does and does not bind, since a district court decision is persuasive, not precedent. The structural point: thousands of US police agencies share Flock data, and defendants now have a template for challenging it. One clause of context: lawmakers introduced bills to curb Flock this week (covered 10-06). Give Flock's and the prosecutors' responses and say whether an appeal is expected. The feed entry was a teaser: write only what the fetched page supports. Single source. Dateline the court's city as the report gives it (Oklahoma City, Tulsa or Muskogee). US dateline (3 of 3).

stories.label: Russian attacks kill at least 24, injure more than 130 over past day; rescue efforts continue in Pryluky
stories.summary: At least 24 people were killed and at least 134 injured in Russian attacks across Ukraine in 24 hours, Ukrainian authorities say; 14 of the dead were in one residential building in Pryluky, Chernihiv Oblast, hit by a cruise missile, and at least two died in Kyiv. Lead with the Pryluky building, the count and the rescue still under way, and name the dead where the reports do. The mechanism: say what Russia fired (how many missiles and drones, how many Ukraine says it intercepted), what was hit besides housing (energy sites before winter, if reported), and what Moscow says it was aiming at; attribute every figure to the side giving it. One clause of context: Ukraine's drone attack on the Moscow region that killed two (covered 10-06), counted with the same care. Al Jazeera is the non-Western source. Dateline Pryluky or Kyiv as the reports support; ignore the feed's 'Dnipro' location tag unless the reports place deaths there.

stories.label: US support for Israel continues three years into the genocide in Gaza
stories.summary: Three years to the day after 7 October 2023, US military aid to Israel is still flowing. Lead with what Al Jazeera documents: how much Washington has sent since the war began, through which channels (the standing aid agreement, supplemental packages, arms sales cleared past Congress), and what has been delivered in the past year. The mechanism: say which US laws condition arms transfers on humanitarian conduct and how each administration has declined to apply them, so the reader sees why the supply has not stopped. Who it lands on: Palestinians in Gaza, with the death toll as reported and attributed, and the Israelis killed on 7 October and since, counted with the same care. Second strand, in one or two sentences: the anniversary falls three weeks before Israel's 27 October election, and Netanyahu's opponents are pressing reports that he received warnings before the attack, which his office denies (RT and The Indian Express carry this; attribute anything from RT to 'Russian state broadcaster RT'). Do not repeat the NatCon speech covered this morning. Al Jazeera is the regional outlet. Dateline Gaza: US policy datelined where it lands, not a US dateline.

stories.label: Yemen's Houthis attack Aden airport; Saudi forces down missile near Riyadh
stories.summary: Follow-up to the 10-06 pieces on the strikes on two Saudi airports and the separatist-led coalition advance (one clause). The new development: Yemen's internationally recognised government says the Houthis fired ballistic missiles and drones at Aden International Airport, the main airport under its control, and Saudi Arabia says it intercepted another missile north of Riyadh. Lead with the Aden strike: what hit, casualties and damage as reported, and whether flights stopped. The mechanism: Aden's airport is the government side's main civilian link to the outside world for travel, medical evacuation and aid, so hitting it carries the war from the front lines to the lifeline of the south, while a missile reaching the Riyadh area shows the Houthis' range into the Saudi capital; say what the Houthis claim and what they say they were aiming at, and what the coalition has done in reply, with Yemeni civilian casualties on every side counted with the same care. Attribute each claim to the side making it. Al Jazeera is the regional outlet and the only source. Dateline Aden.

stories.label: Officials approve island residents’ demand to remain, Staying on Warraq movement says
stories.summary: Residents of Warraq Island, the Nile island in Giza that the Egyptian state has been trying to clear for a development scheme, say officials have agreed to a 'house-for-a-house' arrangement that lets them stay on the land; the Staying on Warraq movement, formed in August, announced it on Tuesday, and no government agency has yet confirmed it. Lead with the concession and that it rests on the movement's word alone. The mechanism: say what the state's plan for the island is and who is behind it, what residents were offered before (compensation and relocation off the island), how the movement negotiated and with whom, and what 'house-for-a-house' would bind the state to. One or two sentences of history as Mada Masr gives it: the years of demolitions, the security siege and the residents killed or jailed. Who it lands on: the tens of thousands of islanders whose homes sit on land the state wants. Attribute the agreement to the movement throughout. Mada Masr is the regional outlet and the only source, doing original reporting. Dateline Warraq Island.

stories.label: Marriage can be dissolved on a woman's initiative on grounds of shiqaq even if cruelty is not proven: SC
stories.summary: Pakistan's Supreme Court ruled on Wednesday that a woman can obtain dissolution of her marriage on the ground of shiqaq (irreconcilable marital discord) under the residuary clause of the Dissolution of Muslim Marriages Act, 1939, even when she has not proven cruelty. Lead with the holding and what it changes. The mechanism for a reader who knows the terms: until now a wife who could not prove a listed ground such as cruelty was usually pushed to khula, where she gives up her dower; say whether the court holds that dissolution for shiqaq leaves her dower intact, which Quranic and juristic reasoning the bench relied on, what the facts of the case were and what the lower courts had decided, and which judges sat. The precedent binds every family court in the country. Who it lands on: women in failing marriages who could not meet the evidentiary bar for cruelty or afford to forfeit mahr. Explain shiqaq, khula and dower in a clause each; state only what the judgment says, as Dawn reports it. Dawn is the regional outlet and the only source. Dateline Islamabad.

stories.label: Syria Set to Emerge as Hormuz Bypass Option for Iraq's Crude Oil
stories.summary: Iraq has asked Syria to carry its crude overland to a Mediterranean port, with a stream of trucks being lined up, so that exports can avoid the Strait of Hormuz. Lead with the request and the route: from which Iraqi fields, to which Syrian port, and how many barrels a day trucks can move against what Iraq shipped through the Gulf before the war. The mechanism: nearly all of Iraq's revenue is oil that leaves through the Strait of Hormuz, the old Kirkuk-Banias pipeline has been dead for decades, so Baghdad is improvising a land bridge by tanker truck through a country still rebuilding from its own war; say what Damascus gains (transit fees, fuel, leverage), what it costs per barrel, and what stands in the way (security on the road, sanctions, capacity). Name the series plainly: ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and the price of Brent crude; Middle East Monitor reports on why traffic through the strait has been rising and how Iran might respond, so give the traffic picture as it states it. One clause of context: Iraq devalued the dinar this week for the same reason (covered this morning). Who it lands on: Iraqis whose salaries depend on those exports. The FT item is a film; use it only for facts the other two support. Bloomberg may be paywalled: write only what the fetched pages support. Middle East Monitor is the regional outlet. Dateline Baghdad or Damascus as the reports support.

stories.label: US 30-Year Yields Return to 2002 High With Crude Back Above $100
stories.summary: The 30-year US Treasury yield is back at its highest since 2002 as Brent crude climbs above $100 a barrel, and the sell-off has spread to Europe, pushing the UK 30-year gilt yield back to 6%. Lead with the two numbers and the cause the reports give: oil pushed up by the war and the attacks on tankers, feeding fears of faster inflation and more interest-rate increases. The mechanism: a long bond's yield is what lenders demand to hold government debt for decades, so when oil lifts expected inflation and central banks tighten, every indebted government pays more to borrow, and mortgages and corporate loans priced off those yields follow; the FT explains why yields are this high, so give its reasons (deficits, inflation, central banks) as it states them. Name the series plainly: the US 10-year Treasury yield, Brent crude, and the Fed's policy rate under Kevin Warsh; give each level only as reported. Who it lands on: borrowers everywhere, and the developing countries whose dollar debt reprices with Treasuries; one clause linking India's rate rise and France's bond stress (both covered this morning). Both sources may be paywalled: write only what the fetched pages support. Dateline New York. US dateline (1 of 3).

stories.label: Bitcoin slips below $84,000 as oil rally hits crypto, layer-2 tokens lead losses: Crypto Markets Today
stories.summary: Bitcoin fell below $84,000 after Iran stepped up attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and Brent crude rallied, and $547 million of leveraged crypto positions were liquidated, CoinDesk reports. Lead with the chain of cause: a strike on shipping, an oil spike, and forced selling in an asset sold as a hedge against exactly this. The mechanism: say why bitcoin fell with risk assets instead of rising like a haven (leverage, and higher oil meaning higher rates), who was liquidated and on which side of the trade. The second fact is structural and belongs high: Abstract, the Pudgy Penguins network, became the second Ethereum layer-2 to shut down in a week, and Optimism's OP token fell 10%; say what a layer-2 is in one clause, why two have closed (fees, users, funding, as reported), and what happens to users' funds. Name the series plainly: bitcoin and Brent crude; give levels only as CoinDesk does. Who it lands on: retail holders trading with borrowed money. This is a daily markets column: take the facts and drop the trading commentary and forecasts. Single source. No dateline: a market report.

stories.label: Conflict in the Red Sea is forcing cloud giants to find a new route for the internet
stories.summary: Google, Meta and Microsoft are said to be securing expensive overland routes for internet traffic because fighting around Yemen threatens the submarine cables that connect Europe and Asia through the Red Sea. Lead with the rerouting and who is paying for it. The mechanism for a technical reader: most Europe-Asia data crosses a handful of cables laid through the Bab el-Mandeb strait and up the Red Sea, a single corridor now inside a war zone where cables have been cut before and repair ships cannot safely work; say which cables are at risk, what share of traffic they carry, which land routes are being bought (through Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Turkey or Israel, as reported), what they cost against sea capacity, and what latency or capacity is lost. The structural point: the physical internet has chokepoints in the same straits as oil, and only the largest cloud companies can afford to route around them. Who it lands on: users and businesses in East Africa, the Gulf and South Asia whose connectivity depends on those cables and who have no private alternative. The feed entry was a teaser, so write only what the fetched page supports and attribute what is 'said' to the sources Rest of World names. Single-source original reporting; no regional outlet in the feed carried it. Dateline as the report supports (Aden, Jeddah or none): a Red Sea story, not a US dateline.

stories.label: Senate passes healthcare cybersecurity bill after 190 million impacted by Change Healthcare breach
stories.summary: The US Senate passed the Health Care Cybersecurity and Resiliency Act of 2026 by unanimous consent last week, a response to the Change Healthcare breach that exposed the data of 190 million people. Lead with the vote and the number. The mechanism for a technical reader: say what the bill would actually require of hospitals, insurers and their vendors (the report says it may expand federal cyber requirements: name them, such as multi-factor authentication, incident reporting deadlines, audits), who would enforce it and with what penalties or funding, and how the Change Healthcare attack worked, where one clearinghouse without a basic control took down payments across the US health system. Accountability: say what UnitedHealth, Change's owner, paid or was penalised, and what the bill leaves voluntary. State what is still needed for it to become law (the House, the president). The feed entry was a teaser: write only what the fetched page supports. Single source. Dateline Washington. US dateline (2 of 3).

stories.label: Google's Power Deal Fuels Fresh Interest in Nuclear Stocks
stories.summary: Google has signed a new long-term agreement with Constellation Energy, the largest US nuclear operator, to supply electricity for its data centres. Lead with the deal itself, not the share prices: how many megawatts, from which plant or plants (Pennsylvania is tagged), for how many years, and whether it is existing output, a restart or new capacity. The mechanism for a technical reader: AI data centres need constant power at a scale the grid cannot add quickly, so the largest technology companies are contracting whole nuclear plants directly; say what that does to supply and prices for other customers on the same grid and what regulators have said about such arrangements, only as the report gives it. One clause for the market reaction. The source is an investment-site summary: take the facts of the agreement, attribute them to the companies, and drop the stock commentary and any recommendations. If the page gives no terms of the deal, drop the story. Single source. Dateline as the report supports (the plant's location). US dateline (3 of 3).

stories.label: PFAS may raise blood pressure during pregnancy. Who is at risk?
stories.summary: A new study links exposure to PFAS, the 'forever chemicals' found in drinking water, food packaging and non-stick coatings, to higher blood pressure during pregnancy, and identifies which women are most at risk. Lead with the finding and its size, as the study gives it. The mechanism for a technical reader: say how exposure was measured (blood levels of which compounds), in how many women and where, what outcome was tracked (blood pressure, gestational hypertension, pre-eclampsia), how large the association is, what biological route the authors propose, and which groups carry the higher risk and why. State the limits: an association in an observational study is not proof of cause, and say so in the authors' terms. Who it lands on: pregnant women who cannot choose their water supply, set against the manufacturers and regulators who decide what is in it. The feed entry was a teaser and Phys.org carries a press summary: name the journal and institutions, attribute claims to the researchers, add no figure the page does not give, and drop the story if the page yields too little. Give the article a dateline and location: the city of the lead institution as the page states it.

stories.label: Libyan fishers lament foreign trawling
stories.summary: Bottom trawling for deep-water shrimp off Libya's coast, much of it by foreign vessels, is degrading the seabed ecosystems that Libyan small-scale fishers depend on, and limiting it could let them rebuild, Dialogue Earth reports. Lead with the evidence: what the research or catch data cited show about the decline, over what period, and what recovery restricted trawling has produced elsewhere. The mechanism for a technical reader: say how a bottom trawl damages the seabed and the food web above it, which species and depths are targeted, whose fleets are fishing (name the flag states as the report does), under what licences or in the absence of them, and why a divided Libyan state cannot police its own waters. Who it lands on: Libyan coastal fishers, named and quoted as the report does, against industrial fleets landing the shrimp for European markets. State what the scientists say is not yet known. If the page turns out to be a feature with no data behind it, write only the documented facts and keep it short. Single specialist source; no Libyan or regional outlet in the feed carried it. Dateline Tripoli or the port the report names.

stories.label: Trump to speak to Putin about plague lab death in Russia
stories.summary: Follow-up to the 10-06 piece on Russia denying anti-plague measures after a worker at the Irkutsk anti-plague institute died (one clause). The new development: the matter has moved to head-of-state level. Trump says he will speak to Putin about the death, that 'we are in very deep discussions', and that he may report back within days, as the BBC gives it. Lead with that escalation and what Washington is asking for. The mechanism: only Russia holds the laboratory records and samples that would settle whether this was plague, so outside governments can get an answer only by political pressure; say what Russia has published and what it denies (Al Jazeera), what the WHO has said or asked for, how many people are quarantined and on whose count, and what the official cause of death is (pneumonia). State no cause beyond the official one, and attribute the 'pneumonic plague' question to those raising it; the News18 item is a video explainer, use it only for facts the other two support. Who it lands on: the people of Irkutsk and Russia's Central Asian neighbours, who depend on that disclosure. Dateline Irkutsk or Moscow as the reports support: the event is in Russia, not a US dateline.

stories.label: NatCon 2026 in Israel: Coming home?
stories.summary: Israel's finance minister, Bezalel Smotrich, told the National Conservatism Conference in Jerusalem on Tuesday that 'Palestinian nationalism is a fiction', that there 'cannot be any rights in the land of Israel for a people that do not exist', and that Gazans should be encouraged to 'voluntarily migrate' to Muslim states. Lead with the speech: a serving minister who controls the budget and much of West Bank civil administration, speaking on the eve of the third anniversary of 7 October and three weeks before Israel's 27 October election, denying a people's existence in front of American allies. Quote him exactly as the report does. The mechanism: he paired it with a pitch to move US support from congressional aid to contractual integration inside the Pentagon, 'from dependence to partnership', so say what that proposal is and who in the US was in the room (Heritage Foundation president Kevin Roberts spoke). Who it lands on: Palestinians in Gaza, where the report gives more than 74,000 killed (attribute the figure). Responsible Statecraft is an advocacy-forward outlet and the only source: state as fact only what was said from the stage and who attended, attribute every characterisation of the conference to the outlet or to the named critic (Curt Mills), and leave its commentary out. No regional outlet in the feed carried the speech. Dateline Jerusalem.

stories.label: East Sussex couple held in Iran seen by UK officials after 112 days
stories.summary: Lindsay and Craig Foreman, a British couple held in Iran for more than 20 months and sentenced to 10 years on espionage charges they deny, have been visited by UK officials at Evin Prison for the first time in 112 days, their family says. Lead with the visit and the gap before it. The mechanism: consular access is the only window a government has on its detained citizens, and Iran granted none for nearly four months while British bases host the US bombers flying in the war on Iran; say what the family reports about the couple's health and conditions, what the Foreign Office says, what Iran alleges and what evidence it has made public, and where any appeal stands. Who holds power: Iran's judiciary over the couple, and London over what it is willing to trade. Attribute the espionage charge to the Iranian court and the denial to the couple; state neither as fact. Single source, and no Iranian or regional outlet in the feed carried it. Dateline Tehran.

stories.label: Why Bagram Air Base Remains a Target Five Years After U.S. Exited Afghanistan
stories.summary: Viral videos and online commentary claim US forces have quietly retaken Bagram, the air base north of Kabul that was the centre of the 20-year occupation; Drop Site examines the claim. Lead with what the reporting establishes: whether there is any evidence of a US return, and what the Taliban government and Washington each say. The mechanism: say why Bagram keeps coming back as a prize (its runways, its position near China, Iran and Central Asia, and what US officials have said publicly about wanting it), who is spreading the claim, and what a real attempt would require. Who it lands on: Afghans, for whom Bagram was also the site of a US detention centre, as the report documents. The feed entry carried only a one-line summary, so write only what the fetched page supports, state no troop presence as fact unless Drop Site confirms it, and drop the story if the page is paywalled. Single-source original reporting; no regional outlet in the feed carried it. Dateline Bagram or Kabul as the report supports: an Afghanistan story, not a US dateline.

stories.label: ECB's Moulin Says Conditions for France Intervention Aren't Met
stories.summary: The European Central Bank will not step in to calm France's bond market: Emmanuel Moulin, the Bank of France governor and ECB Governing Council member, called the situation 'complicated and serious' but said the conditions for intervention are not met, because 'the ECB is not there to deal with the fiscal problems of countries'. Lead with the refusal and what it leaves France facing. The mechanism: the ECB has a tool for buying a member's bonds when its borrowing costs rise out of line, but only for a country following the EU's fiscal rules, so a minority government that cannot pass a budget gets no backstop and must pay what the market asks; give French yields and the spread over Germany, and what set off the sell-off, as the reports state them. Name the series plainly: the ECB's policy rate stays where it is, and the euro moved with the stress (give the move only as reported). Who it lands on: French taxpayers through debt service, and the public services the budget fight is about (one clause: a quarter of a million people marched over school conditions on 10-06). Reuters is the second source; Bloomberg may be paywalled. The 'England and Wales Cricket Board' tag is a mis-tag of ECB. Dateline Paris.

stories.label: Iraq devalues currency as war and Hormuz closure squeeze cash | The National
stories.summary: Iraq has devalued the dinar again, setting an official rate of 1,500 to the US dollar, according to a document seen by The National, after the finance ministry warned parliament that 'without adjustment, it could not fund the 2026 budget', which includes 100,000 new public jobs. Lead with the new rate, the old one and the size of the cut. The mechanism: Iraq earns nearly all its revenue in dollars from oil shipped through the Strait of Hormuz and pays salaries in dinars, so when ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz is choked by the war, a weaker dinar makes each remaining dollar cover more of the wage bill, and the cost moves to households through the price of imports. Say how far exports and revenue have fallen, what the central bank and parliament did, and how the street rate reacted, as reported. Who it lands on: Iraqis on fixed dinar salaries and pensions, in a country that imports most of its food and goods. The devaluation rests on a document the outlet has seen: attribute it. The National (UAE) is the regional outlet and the only source. Dateline Baghdad.

stories.label: South Korea exports eased Russia fuel crisis caused by drone strikes, Ukraine says
stories.summary: Russia imported more than 176,000 tons of petroleum products from South Korean ports in July and August, easing the fuel shortage caused by Ukrainian drone strikes on its refineries, Ukraine's top sanctions official said on Tuesday. Lead with the tonnage and who is making the claim: it is Kyiv's, so attribute it and give Seoul's and the refiners' replies, or say they gave none. The mechanism: Ukraine's campaign against Russian refineries works only if the lost petrol and diesel cannot be replaced, and a US ally that has joined sanctions on Russia is supplying the replacement by tanker to Russia's Far East (Vladivostok is named); say whether these fuel exports break any sanction or sit in a gap the rules leave open, which companies and ships are involved, and how the cargoes were traced, as Reuters reports. One clause of context: Ukraine's drone attack on the Moscow region and the tanker set ablaze off Sochi (covered 10-06). The structural point is how a sanctions regime leaks through its own members. Single source. Dateline Seoul.

stories.label: Call to scrap Sudan's 'costly' advance customs declaration system
stories.summary: Sudanese importers and customs experts are demanding the cancellation of a new Advance Cargo Declaration system that the customs police have begun extending, saying it will raise import costs and consumer prices and hand a foreign company access to sensitive commercial data. Lead with the system, the fee it adds per shipment and who collects it. The mechanism: an advance declaration makes every importer file and pay through a private contractor before cargo is loaded abroad, so a wartime government short of revenue gains a new charge on everything entering through Port Sudan, and the contractor gains a record of who imports what; name the company and its country, say how the contract was awarded, and give the authorities' justification, as reported. Who it lands on: households in a country at war where much of the food, fuel and medicine is imported and the currency has collapsed. Give the critics' cost estimates as theirs. Radio Dabanga is the regional outlet and the only source, doing original reporting. The 'Autodrome Chaudière' tag is a mis-tag of ACD. Dateline Port Sudan.

stories.label: More biodiversity means stronger, more reliable ecosystem functioning worldwide - Nature Ecology & Evolution
stories.summary: A global meta-analysis in Nature Ecology & Evolution finds that ecosystems with more species do more (grow more biomass, cycle more nutrients) and do it more reliably from year to year, across the world's biomes. The article written on this paper on 10-06 was quarantined and never published, so this is not a repeat. Lead with the size of the effect and how many studies and sites stand behind it. The mechanism for a technical reader: say what 'functioning' and 'stability' measure, why diversity helps (species do different jobs, and when one fails in a bad year another compensates), whether the effect holds in real landscapes as well as experimental plots, and where it is strongest or weakest. Who it lands on: the people who depend on those functions for crops, water and fisheries, set against the documented decline of species. State the limits the authors give. This page is the journal's research briefing: name the journal and the lead institution, attribute claims to the authors, and add no figure the page does not give. Give the article a dateline and location: the city of the lead authors' institution as the page states it.

stories.label: Amazon wildfires are generating ozone that weakens surviving trees' carbon uptake
stories.summary: Ozone formed from Amazon wildfire smoke is significantly reducing the rainforest's ability to absorb carbon dioxide, new research finds: the fires damage the trees they never touch. Lead with that second-order loss and the size of it, as the study gives it. The mechanism for a technical reader: fire emissions react in sunlight to form ground-level ozone, which enters leaves through their pores and damages the machinery of photosynthesis, so trees downwind take up less CO2; say how the team measured or modelled it, over what area and which fire seasons, and how the loss compares with the carbon released by the fires themselves. Who it lands on: the people of the Amazon basin breathing the same ozone, and a climate that relies on the forest as a sink; who sets the fires (land clearing) only as the report says. State the limits the authors give. Phys.org carries a press summary and the feed entry was thin: name the journal and institutions, attribute claims to the researchers, add no figure the page does not give, and drop the story if the page yields too little. Give the article a dateline and location: the Amazon city or region the study names, otherwise the lead institution's city.

stories.label: Christa Pike Regains Consciousness After Her Failed Execution
stories.summary: Christa Pike, the Tennessee death row inmate who survived two doses of a lethal injection drug in a botched execution last week and left the chamber in an ambulance, is conscious and speaking, her lawyers say. Lead with her condition and the question it opens: can a state try a second time to kill a prisoner it failed to kill, and who decides (the courts, the governor, the corrections department), as the reports give it. The mechanism: say what drug and protocol Tennessee used (pentobarbital is tagged), what went wrong as far as officials or her lawyers have said (Hindustan Times reports a blood-clotting condition, thrombocytosis, as a possible factor: attribute it), what the state has disclosed and what it is withholding, and what legal filings are pending. Accountability: the state holds every record of what happened in the chamber. Give the victim of Pike's crime and her family the same care as Pike: name her and say what the family has said, if reported. State nothing about the execution itself beyond what the sources give. The 'Pike County, Kentucky' tag is a mis-tag. Al Jazeera is the non-Western source. Dateline Nashville or as the reports support. US dateline (1 of 3).

stories.label: Rahul, Priyanka Gandhi booked for Akashvani Bhawan entry
stories.summary: Follow-up to the 10-06 piece on Congress planning a nationwide campaign for the removal of India's Chief Election Commissioner over deleted voters (one clause). The new development: Delhi Police detained opposition INDIA bloc MPs, including Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, during a march on the Election Commission on Tuesday, and have now registered a case against them over entering Akashvani Bhawan, the state broadcaster's building. Lead with the detentions and the case: who was held, for how long, and under what provisions they are booked. The mechanism: the opposition wants Gyanesh Kumar removed over the voter-roll revision and the deletions it produced (give the figure and whose it is, as the reports state), and the police answering to the central government have turned a protest about the electoral roll into a criminal case against the opposition's leaders; say what the Election Commission and the government reply. Who it lands on: the voters struck from the rolls, and which communities they are, only as the reports document. All three sources are Indian outlets with differing leanings: take facts common to them and attribute each side's characterisation. Dateline New Delhi.

stories.label: India's central bank hikes rates for the first time since 2023 as inflation creeps up
stories.summary: The Reserve Bank of India raised its repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.5% on Wednesday, its first increase since 2023, as inflation climbs. Lead with the decision, the new rate and the vote if given. The mechanism: say what is driving Indian inflation as the bank states it (Mint points to rising Brent crude and higher US bond yields; India imports most of its oil, so the war premium on crude arrives as fuel and food prices), what the bank forecasts for inflation and growth, and what it signalled about further increases. Who it lands on: borrowers with floating-rate home and business loans, and households already paying more for fuel; give the market reaction in one clause (the Sensex fell about 529 points, per Mint). Place it in one clause among the other central banks now tightening, as CNBC does. The 'Run batted in' and 'Monetary Policy Committee (United Kingdom)' tags are mis-tags of RBI and MPC. Dateline Mumbai.

stories.label: Oman evacuates injured crew from attacked tanker in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Oman's air force evacuated 10 crew from the Panamanian-flagged oil tanker On Peace after it was struck on Tuesday about 9 nautical miles off the Omani port of Limah in the Strait of Hormuz, setting off a fire; India says 12 crew were injured, 11 of them Indian, and has condemned the attack on the Dubai-owned ship (owner Onex, per The National). Lead with the strike, the injured seafarers and who they are. Attribution is the story: say what hit the ship (a projectile, as reported), who Oman, India and the owner blame, if anyone, and what Iran says; state no attribution as fact. The mechanism: this is ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, the passage for roughly a fifth of the world's oil, and each strike raises insurance and the price of Brent crude; give the oil price move and the traffic or insurance effect only as the reports state them. Who bears it: crews from India and other labour-exporting countries, on ships flagged in Panama and owned in the Gulf, which is why New Delhi is the government protesting. The 'Ministry of Defence (United Kingdom)' and 'Montana' tags are mis-tags (Omani Ministry of Defence; MT is motor tanker). The National (UAE) is the regional outlet, merged in from its own feed entry. Dateline Muscat or Khasab as the reports support: an Oman story.

stories.label: Ship ablaze near Sochi, huge plume of smoke rising over sea - photos
stories.summary: A Liberian-flagged oil tanker with an all-Indian crew caught fire off the Russian Black Sea city of Sochi on the evening of 6 October after what the Guardian and NDTV report as a Ukrainian drone strike; Ukrainska Pravda's first report rests on local Telegram footage. Lead with the burning tanker, the crew and their condition, and who says what struck it: attribute the drone strike to whoever claims or reports it (Kyiv, Russian officials, the outlets) and state it as fact only if both sides confirm. The mechanism: Russia exports much of its crude through its Black Sea ports, and strikes on tankers there aim at the revenue that funds the war, while the people on board are third-country seafarers; say what the ship was carrying and for whom, whether it is linked to the sanctioned 'shadow fleet' if reported, and any spill. This is a separate attack from the two ships hit in Bulgaria's economic zone (covered 10-06, one clause), and the Bulgaria, Varna and Rumen Radev tags are bleed from that event: do not merge the facts. Mention the effect on oil prices or Black Sea insurance only as the reports give it. Dateline Sochi.

stories.label: US firm gets $2.9bn sub deal after boss joins war study with Musk
stories.summary: Anduril Industries, the California defence technology firm, won a $2.9bn deal to build components for the US Navy's Virginia-class submarines and said it will invest $3.7bn in a new shipyard in Maryland, shortly after its boss joined a government war study alongside Elon Musk, Al Jazeera reports. Lead with the contract, its value and the sequence Al Jazeera draws: the appointment, then the award. The mechanism: say what the study is and who named its members, how the contract was awarded (competed or sole-source, as reported), and what Anduril, which has never built submarine parts, will make; The War Zone supplies the industrial context, that the Navy is missing its submarine delivery goals and is looking beyond its two established yards. Accountability: executives advising the government on how to fight are the same people selling it the equipment; give the company's and the Navy's replies, and state no impropriety as fact. The 'Anduril (workflow engine)' tag is a mis-tag. Dateline Baltimore. US dateline (2 of 3).

stories.label: The world's oyster reefs could add $12 trillion to planetary health each year—if they were better managed
stories.summary: A new study calculates the potential 'gross ecosystem product' of the world's oyster reefs, the ecological counterpart of GDP, and arrives at about $12 trillion a year in goods and services, a value the authors say is vastly underestimated and mostly unrealised because the reefs are degraded. Lead with the figure and what it is: a modelled potential, reachable only if reefs are restored and protected, not a measurement of what they deliver today. The mechanism for a technical reader: say what services are counted (water filtration, coastal protection, fisheries habitat, nutrient and carbon cycling, as the paper lists them), how each is priced, how much of the world's historic reef area survives, and what restoration would cost against the return. State the limits the authors give, and that ecosystem valuations depend heavily on the prices assumed. Name the journal and the institutions. Phys.org carries a press summary: attribute claims to the researchers and add no figure the page does not give. No dateline: reporting on a published study.

stories.label: Sharing AI progress in mathematics
stories.summary: OpenAI published an account of its models' progress in mathematics, which drew 634 points and 577 comments on Hacker News. Lead with the most concrete claim on OpenAI's page: which problems or results, whether any is a new proof or an open problem, and who checked it. The mechanism for a technical reader: say how the results were produced (which model, how much human guidance, formal verification in a proof assistant or review by mathematicians), what was released that others can inspect (proofs, transcripts, code), and what the company says the system still cannot do. Every claim is the vendor's own: attribute it to OpenAI, say whether independent mathematicians are named as having verified the work, and say plainly if they are not. The source is a company announcement, so write only what the fetched page supports and add nothing from memory. No dateline: a company publication, not a US-datelined event.

stories.label: South Korean president calls for creation of tools that stop all cyber-attacks
stories.summary: South Korea's president, Lee Jae Myung, told his cabinet it is time to build AI-powered defensive tools against AI-wielding attackers, after a run of personal-data leaks at financial and public institutions. Lead with what he ordered and what prompted it: name the breaches The Register cites and how many people's data they exposed. The mechanism for a technical reader: say what the government actually committed (a programme, a budget, an agency, a deadline) as against what is aspiration, and what 'stop all attacks' can and cannot mean in practice, as the report puts it. The structural point: one of the world's most connected countries keeps losing citizens' data from the institutions that hold most of it, and the state is answering with a tooling programme. If the page is a regional roundup, write only the South Korea item; the Australia, Medicare and OpenAI tags come from other items on it. Drop the outlet's jokey tone. Single source. Dateline Seoul.

stories.label: Allies of President Donald Trump are trying to sideline AI safety advocates
stories.summary: The Washington Post reports that allies of President Trump are working to sideline advocates of AI safety. The feed carried only the headline, inside a cluster of unrelated AI stock items, so write only what the fetched page supports: who the allies are, who they are trying to push out and from where (agencies, advisory bodies, standards work, funding), by what means, and what evidence the Post has (documents, named sources). The mechanism to draw out if the report gives it: who sets the rules for AI in the US is being decided by removing one side of the argument from the rooms where rules are written, to the benefit of the companies that build the models. Give the named parties' replies. If the page cannot be fetched in full, drop the story and do not write from the headline. Single source. Dateline Washington. US dateline (3 of 3).

stories.label: Amid Midterm Crunch, Trump Advisers Took Time to Help Russia-Aligned Government
stories.summary: Two of Trump's top political advisers spent last week in the Balkans working for the pro-Russian leadership of Republika Srpska, the Serb entity of Bosnia and Herzegovina, as its election was held. Lead with who the advisers are, who paid them and what they did, as the Times documents it. The mechanism: private consulting by people inside a president's political operation gives a foreign client access that looks like US backing, in a country where Milorad Dodik's secessionism threatens the Dayton settlement that ended the Bosnian war; say what US policy on Dodik formally is (sanctions, as reported) and whether the advisers registered as foreign agents. Who it lands on: Bosniaks, the survivors of the 1990s genocide, who depend on that settlement. One clause of context: the Serb leader's election win (covered 10-05). Give the advisers' and the White House's replies. Single-source original reporting. Dateline Banja Luka or Sarajevo as the report supports: the event is in Bosnia, not a US dateline.

stories.label: Ex-US spy found with $40m in gold bars pleads guilty to wire fraud
stories.summary: David Rush, 49, a former CIA official arrested in May with more than $40m in gold bars at his home, pleaded guilty to wire fraud under a deal requiring nearly $200m in restitution. Lead with the plea and the two numbers. The mechanism is the accountability story: say how an intelligence officer could take that much from his employer, through what scheme and over how long, what controls failed inside an agency whose budget is secret, and what the plea deal leaves uncharged or unexplained, as the BBC reports it. Give the sentence he faces and the date, and what the CIA has said or that it has not commented. The 'Rush (band)' tag is a mis-tag. Single source. US dateline (1 of 3).

stories.label: Southern Separatist Fighters Are Driving Saudi Gains Against the Houthis
stories.summary: Follow-up to the pieces on the Mecca alliance and the strikes on Saudi airports (one clause). The new development: the Houthis say they repelled a coalition offensive near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait and fired 10 missiles at coalition forces, while Yemen's government says its troops are advancing. That exchange is carried by the Russian state news agency TASS and must be attributed to each side, not stated as fact. What New Lines adds is who is doing the fighting: the Saudi gains followed an unusual Saudi-Emirati meeting in Riyadh and rely on the UAE-backed Giants Brigades, southern separatists whose aim is an independent south, not a restored Yemeni government. Lead with that mechanism: Riyadh is winning ground with a force whose loyalties decide who holds the coast above one of the world's main shipping lanes, so say what the brigades have taken, what the separatists want in return, and what it means for ship traffic through Bab el-Mandeb. Yemeni civilian casualties and displacement as reported, counted with the same care on every side. No regional outlet in the feed carried this. Dateline Aden or the front as the reports support: a Yemen story.

stories.label: Court halts Gqeberha evictions as families resist move into vandalised units
stories.summary: A court has halted evictions at Airport Valley in Gqeberha after the Nelson Mandela Bay municipality bulldozed 14 homes on 28 September while public order police fired stun grenades and rubber bullets; families refuse to move into the vandalised units offered instead. Lead with the order and the demolitions it stops, and name residents as Daily Maverick does (Nomboniso Ntunduse's belongings were still inside her shack). The mechanism: South African law bars eviction without a court order and requires the state to provide adequate alternative accommodation, so say whether the municipality had an order, what condition the replacement units are in, why the land is being cleared, and what the court requires next. Give the municipality's and the police's replies. The wider pattern in one clause, only if the report gives it: informal settlement clearances in South African cities. Single-source ground reporting. Dateline Gqeberha.

stories.label: Tories took £1.3 million from firm linked to Israeli settlements
stories.summary: Britain's Conservative Party has taken £1.3 million from JCB, the digger maker whose machines Amnesty International says are 'part of the machinery of ethnic cleansing' in illegal West Bank settlements. Lead with the sum, the period and the donor, which rest on public donation records, and say so. The mechanism: JCB equipment sold through an Israeli dealer is used to demolish Palestinian homes and build settlements, and the company's owners are among the largest funders of a party that sets UK policy on arms and trade with Israel; say what Amnesty documented and where, what UK and OECD guidance on business in occupied territory requires, and what JCB and the Conservatives reply, or that they gave none. Who it lands on: the Palestinian families whose homes were demolished, as documented. Declassified UK is an advocacy-forward outlet and the only source: attribute the characterisation to Amnesty and the outlet, and state as fact only the donation figures and what Amnesty's report records. Dateline London.

stories.label: Colombia’s world-first recognition of rivers as war victims endangered
stories.summary: Colombia's transitional justice system has formally recognised several rivers as victims of the armed conflict, a world first, and the state institution that did it now faces an uncertain future. Lead with the recognition and the threat to it: which rivers, which body granted the status (name it as the report does), and what puts it at risk (mandate expiry, budget, politics, as reported). The mechanism: victim status turns environmental damage from war (oil spilled from bombed pipelines, mercury from illegal gold mining, coca processing) into harm that perpetrators must answer for and repair, so say what reparations have been ordered and who speaks for a river in court. Who it lands on: the Indigenous and Afro-Colombian communities that live on those rivers. This is law and politics, not a science finding, so it is filed under politics although the feed tags it science. Single specialist source. Dateline Bogotá or the region named.

stories.label: Social Media is Fertile Ground for Illegal Mining Players in Peru
stories.summary: Posing as a would-be miner, InSight Crime answered a Facebook advert offering land with mining permits in Peru's Madre de Dios region and documented how the trade works. Lead with the sting and what was offered, at what price. The mechanism: Peru's formalisation permits are meant to let informal miners go legal, but a permit holder can pass off illegally dug gold as legitimate output, so permits are sold and rented on social media as a front for illegal mining and a way to launder black-market gold; say how the registry works, how many permits exist, what experts say about enforcement, and what Meta's rules are and whether it responded. With gold at high prices, one clause on why the incentive is growing, only as the report gives it. Who it lands on: the Amazon forest and rivers poisoned with mercury and the Indigenous communities in Madre de Dios. Single-source original investigation. Dateline Puerto Maldonado, or none if the report does not place it.

stories.label: HBO Max, Paramount+, and Discovery+ "will unify into a single service
stories.summary: Paramount Skydance completed its acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery on Tuesday and said HBO Max, Paramount+ and Discovery+ will be merged into one service. Lead with the closing of the deal, its value if Ars gives it, and what one owner now controls: two film studios, the streaming services, and the news and cable networks named in the report. The mechanism: streaming has not paid for the content it carries, so scale is bought by merger, and subscribers end up with fewer competitors and one price; say what happens to existing subscriptions and prices, what regulators required for approval, how much debt the combined company carries and what job cuts are announced, as reported. Accountability in one clause: who owns and funds Paramount Skydance, as Ars states it. This is a merger story, filed under economy. Single source. US dateline (2 of 3).

stories.label: Hydrothermal vents supply a geochemical precursor of ATP that could have powered early life
stories.summary: Biologists at Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf report in The FEBS Journal that phosphite and palladium, both found naturally in hydrogen-producing hydrothermal vents, can act as an inorganic precursor of ATP. Lead with the question it answers: every living cell runs on phosphate as its energy currency, and nobody has shown where that energy came from before there were enzymes to make it. The mechanism for a technical reader: say what reaction the team ran, under what conditions, what the metal does as a catalyst, what energy-rich phosphate compound it yields, and how that maps onto the oldest metabolic pathways. State the limits: a laboratory demonstration of a plausible route, not proof of what happened four billion years ago, and the phrase 'could have' is the authors' own. The source is a university press release carried by Phys.org: name the journal, attribute the claims to the researchers, and quote no independent scientist unless the page does. No dateline.

stories.label: Metal detectorist finds second Bronze Age hoard seven miles from first near Peebles
stories.summary: Mariusz Stepien, the metal detectorist who found the Peebles Hoard, has found a second Bronze Age hoard seven miles away, and it contains mould materials used in casting bronze, which archaeologists say almost never survive. Lead with the find and why the moulds matter: finished objects show what people owned, moulds show where and how they were made. The mechanism: say what the hoard holds, how old it is, how it was excavated and by whom, and what the link between the two hoards could reveal about metalworking and exchange in Bronze Age Scotland, as the researchers put it. State what is not yet known: analysis has only begun. Give what happens to the find under Scottish treasure law if the BBC says. Single source. Dateline Peebles.

stories.label: Hackers obtain counterfeit TLS certificates for Google and other large services
stories.summary: Attackers hijacked three country-code top-level domains, .gh (Ghana), .sl (Sierra Leone) and .as (American Samoa), and used that control to obtain counterfeit TLS certificates for Google and other large organisations, Google said on Tuesday. Lead with the three registries and what was minted. The mechanism for a developer: a certificate authority issues a certificate to whoever proves control of a domain, usually by a DNS or HTTP challenge, so whoever controls the top-level domain's DNS can answer the challenge for every name under it, and the padlock then vouches for an impostor; say how the registries were compromised, which authorities issued the certificates, how the fraud was detected (Certificate Transparency logs, if reported), whether the certificates were used to intercept traffic, and what has been revoked. The structural point: the web's trust rests on small, under-resourced national registries. Say who Google attributes it to only as attribution. Single source. No dateline.

stories.label: OpenAI will watermark ChatGPT outputs by default -- but only in the EU
stories.summary: OpenAI will automatically watermark text generated by ChatGPT in the European Union to comply with the EU AI Act, and will leave the feature off by default everywhere else. Lead with the split: the same product, marked in one jurisdiction and unmarked in the rest. The mechanism for a technical reader: say how a text watermark works as Ars describes it (a statistical bias in word choice detectable by a key holder), how easily paraphrasing or translation removes it, who can run the detector, and whether it covers the API. Accountability: OpenAI has had the technique for years and held it back, so say what the company gave as its reason then and what the law requires now and from what date. Who it lands on: teachers, editors and platforms outside the EU who get no signal. Single source. No dateline: a company policy shaped by EU law, not a US-datelined event.

stories.label: Alleged ATM malware creator appears in Nebraska court after arrest
stories.summary: The alleged author of ATM malware, named Aguirre in the report, appeared in a Nebraska federal court after his arrest; in March he became the first cybercriminal placed on the FBI's Ten Most Wanted Fugitives list. Lead with the court appearance, where and how he was arrested, and the charges. The mechanism for a technical reader: ATM 'jackpotting' malware makes a cash machine dispense its cassettes on command, so say how the malware was installed (physical access, a swapped drive, the network), how many machines and how much money prosecutors attribute to it, and who used it, as the indictment alleges. He is a defendant: state every allegation as the prosecution's and give his plea or his lawyer's reply. Thin feed entry, picked because tech is at its floor and the feed has no other full tech report beyond the two Ars pieces: write only what the fetched page supports. Single source. US dateline (3 of 3).

stories.label: Nobel Prize in Physics Is Awarded to Francis Halzen
stories.summary: Francis Halzen, the Belgian-born physicist behind the IceCube Neutrino Observatory at the South Pole, won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics for the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin. Lead with the prize and the discovery in plain terms: particles that pass through whole planets almost untouched, caught arriving from outside the galaxy. The mechanism for a technical reader: IceCube turns a cubic kilometre of Antarctic ice into a detector, with strings of light sensors frozen deep in it recording the faint blue flash when a neutrino very occasionally strikes an atom; say how the team separated cosmic neutrinos from the flood made in Earth's atmosphere, what sources they have since been traced to, and why neutrinos show what light cannot, since they travel straight from the most violent objects in the universe. Give the academy's citation, the prize money and Halzen's reaction as reported, and note that he is a sole laureate for work built by a collaboration of hundreds, if the reports say so. Al Jazeera is in the cluster. Dateline Stockholm.

stories.label: Quarter million protesters rally across France over school conditions
stories.summary: A quarter of a million people marched across France on Tuesday as unions and teachers joined high-school students blockading schools over learning conditions; hundreds were injured when police answered with tear gas and riot-control rounds. Lead with the turnout (say whose count it is: unions or the interior ministry), the injured on both sides counted with the same care, and what the students are actually demanding (class sizes, buildings, staffing, budget cuts, as reported). The mechanism: a school-level blockade movement became a national strike day once the teaching unions joined, so say what the government has offered and what the budget behind the grievance is. RT's item concerns a teenager whose hand was injured by a police grenade: RT is Russian state media, so use it only if Al Jazeera or the wire copy inside TRT supports the incident, and attribute it. TRT World is Turkish state media; Al Jazeera (a photo report) is the independent source. Dateline Paris.

stories.label: France Tests New Nuclear-Capable Weapon
stories.summary: France test-fired the upgraded M51.3 submarine-launched ballistic missile, without a warhead, from the submarine Le Vigilant, months after pledging to expand its nuclear arsenal. Lead with the test and what is new about the missile as the defence ministry gives it (range, payload, first firing of this version from a submarine). The mechanism: France is the EU's only nuclear power and has offered to extend its deterrent to European allies as confidence in the US guarantee weakens, so say what the expansion pledge was, how many warheads and submarines France has, and what Paris and Moscow said. One clause of context: Lithuania's parliament voted to lift its ban on hosting nuclear weapons (covered 10-06). This is a weapons test, filed under politics, not science (the feed's tag is wrong). Vanguard carries the AFP report. Dateline Paris.

stories.label: Russia denies anti-plague measures after pneumonia death
stories.summary: Follow-up to the 10-05 pieces on the death of a worker at the Irkutsk anti-plague institute, which rested on Russian state media alone (one clause). The new developments: Moscow now denies it has imposed anti-plague measures and says the death is still under investigation, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has called on Russia to be transparent about its findings, and Eurasianet reports the case has rattled Central Asian neighbours. Lead with the denial set against what is known: who died, of what as officially stated (pneumonia), and how many were quarantined. The mechanism: a death inside a laboratory that handles plague is a biosafety question the outside world can only answer with data Russia controls, so say what has and has not been published, what Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and the others have done at their borders or said, and what the WHO has asked for. State no cause of death as fact beyond the official one. This is the first independent sourcing on the story (DW, Eurasianet); TRT World is Turkish state media. A public-health event filed under politics: there is no finding. Dateline Irkutsk or Moscow as the reports support.

stories.label: UK police arrest British national linked to airbase incident
stories.summary: Follow-up to the 10-05 piece on Trump saying terror threats forced US B-1 bombers out of a British base (one clause). The new development is an arrest: Counter Terrorism Police detained a 22-year-old British national on suspicion of a terror offence linked to 'activity that took place close to RAF Fairford' on 27 September, the seventh arrest in the investigation per ABP Live. Lead with the arrest, the offence as police word it, and the running total. The mechanism: Fairford hosts the US bombers flying in the war on Iran, so say what police have and have not disclosed about the incident, who the earlier six are and whether any have been charged, and whether investigators allege a foreign state link or say nothing on it. The arrested are suspects: state no allegation as fact. Al Jazeera is the regional voice. Dateline London.

stories.label: Before UK Greens, who else has equated Zionism with racism?
stories.summary: Members of the Green Party of England and Wales voted at their Brighton conference on Sunday to declare Zionism a form of racism, making it the first major UK party to do so; zuhd.news has not covered the vote. Lead with the vote itself: the motion's wording, the tally if given, and what it commits the party to. Then the precedent both reports reconstruct: UN General Assembly Resolution 3379 said the same in 1975 and was revoked in 1991, and Middle East Eye reports on Britain's role in the lobbying around it; give dates, vote counts and who pushed revocation, as reported. The mechanism: a party polling as a real force adopts as policy a position the UN once held and abandoned, so say what the party leadership, Jewish organisations, Palestinian groups and the government each said, quoting critics and supporters with the same care, and state neither characterisation of Zionism as fact. Both pieces are explainers written around the vote: take the news from them and leave the commentary. Dateline Brighton or London as the reports support.

stories.label: Syndicate submits prosecution complaint regarding Matsda2sh journalists’ torture, Interior Ministry denies claims
